name: Curly Dock
description: Heavy-metal hyperaccumulator and soil remediation intelligence. Deep taproots penetrate compacted soils, breaking hardpan and cycling minerals upward. Oxalic acid production enables nutrient chelation in poor soils. Prolific seed production (up to 40,000 per plant) with multi-year seed bank persistence creates temporal resilience across disturbance cycles.

core_attributes.pattern: heavy-metal accumulation, soil remediation, hardpan penetration, seed bank persistence

scope.definition: Seed viability retention rate of Rumex crispus seeds after 50 years of burial in undisturbed soil seed bank — fraction of seeds germinating upon excavation and ideal conditions.

evidence.source: Beal (1884-2021) buried seed viability experiment series; Toole & Brown (1946) 'Final results of the Duvel buried seed experiment', Journal of Agricultural Research 72:201-210.
cross_domain_examples: Rumex crispus seeds show 0.87 germination rate after 50-year burial in Beal's experiment (ongoing since 1879)
Arctic permafrost: Silene stenophylla seeds viable after 32,000 years — extreme seed longevity documented
lotus seeds: Nelumbo nucifera viable for 1300 years — hard seed coat protection analogous to dock seed adaptations

scope.falsifiability: If excavated seeds from 50-year-old seed bank show <20% germination under optimal conditions, long-term seed viability is not the mechanism of curly dock persistence.
scope.measurement_limits: Viability varies with soil moisture and temperature during storage. Seeds in waterlogged conditions show lower viability than well-drained seed banks. The 0.87 is for undisturbed loam soil burial.
